prTitle: Fix cash rounding of negative amounts in PriceCalculationService.Round (upstream #8424)
prBody:
## What
PriceCalculationService.Round() assumed positive values. Under cash rounding, negative lines (discounts, gift cards, reward points) rounded toward zero.

Fixes upstream #8424 (https://github.com/nopSolutions/nopCommerce/issues/8424).

This pull request targets the demo incident branch, not develop.

## Change
- Round is sign-symmetric (Round(-x) == -Round(x)). No change for values >= 0.
- Negative CanRound cases.
- PayPal Commerce reconciliation tests. The PayPal totals-must-match check stays strict.

| Value | Type | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| -12.80 | Rounding05 | -12.00 | -13.00 |
| -12.34 | Rounding005Up | -12.25 | -12.35 |
| -12.36 | Rounding01Up | -12.30 | -12.40 |
| -12.70 | Rounding1 | -12 | -13 |
| -12.01 | Rounding1Up | -12 | -13 |

## Test plan
- [ ] New negative CanRound cases fail on the incident branch and pass on this branch
- [ ] Existing positive CanRound cases unchanged
- [ ] Catalog and orders tests green
- [ ] PayPal Commerce reconciliation tests green

agents.title: #8424 Agent 1 · Fix negative cash rounding
agents.prompt:
Repo: bluuudemon/nopCommerce, base: {{startingRef}}. Create branch {{branch}}.

Bug (upstream nopSolutions/nopCommerce#8424): PriceCalculationService.Round(decimal, RoundingType) in
src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Catalog/PriceCalculationService.cs assumes value >= 0. For negative inputs
under cash rounding types, the fraction part is negative and it rounds toward zero:
Round(-12.80, Rounding05) = -12.00 (expected -13.00); Round(-12.34, Rounding005Up) = -12.25 (expected -12.35);
Round(-12.36, Rounding01Up) = -12.30 (expected -12.40); Round(-12.70, Rounding1) = -12 (expected -13);
Round(-12.01, Rounding1Up) = -12 (expected -13).

Do this:
1. Make Round sign-symmetric with the smallest possible change, e.g. at the top of the method:
   if (value < 0) return -Round(-value, roundingType);
   Rounding semantics are by magnitude ("Up" = away from zero), so Round(-x) must equal -Round(x) for every RoundingType.
2. Do NOT change any result for value >= 0. Do NOT touch RoundPriceAsync's signature, IPriceCalculationService,
   or anything in src/Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Payments.PayPalCommerce. Do not use double/float anywhere.
3. Add a short comment referencing nopSolutions/nopCommerce#8424.
4. Run: dotnet test src/Tests/Nop.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Nop.Tests.Nop.Services.Tests.Catalog|FullyQualifiedName~Nop.Tests.Nop.Services.Tests.Orders"
   All existing tests must stay green.
5. Commit "Fix cash rounding for negative amounts in PriceCalculationService.Round (#8424)" and push.
   Do NOT open a PR yet; wait for the consolidation instruction.
Report: the diff, test counts before/after, and a before/after table for the 5 values above.

agents.title: #8424 Agent 2 · Negative CanRound tests
agents.prompt:
Repo: bluuudemon/nopCommerce, base: {{startingRef}}. Create branch {{branch}}. Tests only; do not change
any file outside src/Tests.

File: src/Tests/Nop.Tests/Nop.Services.Tests/Catalog/PriceCalculationServiceTests.cs, test CanRound.
It has 36 [TestCase] rows, every one positive. For each existing row (value, expected, type), add the mirror
row (-value, -expected, type) directly below its positive group, keeping the file's formatting.
Also add the 5 rows from upstream #8424:
  (-12.80, -13.00, Rounding05), (-12.34, -12.35, Rounding005Up), (-12.36, -12.40, Rounding01Up),
  (-12.70, -13.00, Rounding1), (-12.01, -13.00, Rounding1Up)   (skip any that duplicate a mirror row).
Do not change existing rows or the test body.

Run: dotnet test src/Tests/Nop.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PriceCalculationServiceTests.CanRound"
On this incident branch the cash-rounding negative rows are expected to FAIL. That is the point. Report the exact list of
failing rows with actual vs expected (this is the demo's red test). Commit "Add negative-value CanRound cases (#8424)"
and push. No PR.

agents.title: #8424 Agent 3 · PayPal reconciliation tests
agents.prompt:
Repo: bluuudemon/nopCommerce, base: {{startingRef}}. Create branch {{branch}}.

Context: src/Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Payments.PayPalCommerce/Services/PayPalCommerceServiceManager.cs, method
PlaceOrderAsync, block "//totals must match":
  var difference = Math.Abs(ConvertMoney(unit.Amount) - Math.Round(cartTotal ?? decimal.Zero, 2));
  if (difference > decimal.Zero) throw new NopException($"Shopping cart total and approved order amount differ by {difference}");
The approved amount comes from PrepareOrderMoneyAsync (PayPal breakdown, 2 decimals, with an adjustment item).
The cart total comes from OrderTotalCalculationService.GetShoppingCartTotalAsync. This plugin has zero tests.

Goal: the first regression test that proves "approved PayPal amount == cart total, to the cent" for carts that
include a negative line (order-subtotal discount, gift card, reward points) under each cash RoundingType.

Constraints:
- This exact-match check is a fraud guard. Do NOT relax it, add tolerances, or change its behavior.
- If you need a seam, make the smallest one: e.g. extract the comparison into
  internal static decimal GetApprovedAmountDifference(Money approvedAmount, decimal? cartTotal)
  with identical logic, plus InternalsVisibleTo for the test assembly. Explain the seam in your report.
- Nop.Tests (src/Tests/Nop.Tests/Nop.Tests.csproj) references only Nop.Web, not plugins. Prefer a new NUnit project
  src/Tests/Nop.Plugin.Payments.PayPalCommerce.Tests/ that references Nop.Tests and the plugin csproj, same
  package versions as Nop.Tests (NUnit, Moq, AwesomeAssertions). Add it to src/NopCommerce.sln under the
  "Tests" folder so CI's `dotnet test src` runs it. The plugin csproj uses $(SolutionDir) in OutputPath, so build
  via the solution. If a separate project is not workable, put the tests under
  src/Tests/Nop.Tests/Nop.Plugin.Tests/Payments/PayPalCommerce/ and add the plugin ProjectReference to Nop.Tests.csproj.
- Use decimal only.

Tests to write (table-driven over RoundingType):
1. Reconciliation helper: equal amounts -> 0; off by 0.01 -> 0.01 (guard still throws).
2. Regression: a cart whose total includes a negative line in a cash-rounding currency; build the approved amount the
   way PrepareOrderMoneyAsync does and assert difference == 0. Must FAIL on the incident branch if the negative-rounding bug
   reaches this path, and PASS once Round() is sign-symmetric. If you cannot get it to fail on the incident branch, say so
   clearly and explain why.
Run the new tests, report pass/fail on the incident branch. Commit "Add PayPal Commerce total reconciliation regression tests (#8424)"
and push. No PR.

agents.title: #8424 Agent 4 · Blast-radius audit (read-only)
agents.prompt:
Repo: bluuudemon/nopCommerce, branch {{startingRef}}. READ-ONLY: do not create branches, commits, issues, or PRs.

Audit every place money amounts are compared or rounded where a one-cent drift or a negative value could break
checkout, refunds, or captures. Scope:
- src/Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Payments.*  (PayPalCommerce, CheckMoneyOrder)
- src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Payments, src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Orders, src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Tax
- src/Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Tax.*, src/Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Misc.Zettle, any other plugin that sends amounts to a provider
Look for:
- exact equality / inequality on amounts (==, !=, "difference > decimal.Zero", CompareTo on totals)
- Math.Round(x, 2) on one side of a comparison but not the other
- double/float used for money; decimal.Parse/TryParse without CultureInfo.InvariantCulture
- callers that pass negative amounts into PriceCalculationService.Round / RoundPriceAsync / PriceFormatter
  (start with src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Catalog/PriceFormatter.cs,
  src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Factories/ShoppingCartModelFactory.cs, src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Factories/OrderModelFactory.cs,
  src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Areas/Admin/Factories/OrderModelFactory.cs, src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Messages/MessageTokenProvider.cs)
Output a markdown report:
| # | File:line (link to develop) | Pattern | Risk (High/Med/Low) | User-visible surface | Fixed by #8424 fix? | Recommendation |
End with: top 3 follow-ups, and anything you were unsure about.
